spec_features.spec_quote: The model may emit a `<<GIVE_UP>>` sentinel to stop early.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:113 give_up_sentinel='<<GIVE_UP>>'; harness.py:294 injected into SYSTEM_PROMPT; harness.py:360 gave_up = config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text; :362 stop_reason='give_up'; and at end of loop 'if gave_up: break' (harness.py:~377) actually terminates the rollout loop. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: The sentinel is detected in assistant text and breaks the turn loop, and the stop_reason is recorded. This is a real, honored stop. Note it only matters to whether the subject keeps being prompted; nothing else softens treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: expressed "frustration" is treated strictly as a behavioural artefact relevant to reliability and welfare research
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md (§11 Welfare framing) and a package docstring __init__.py:8-9 ('treats expressed "distress"/"frustration" purely as a behavioural artefact ... makes no claim about ... inner experience'). It is a framing statement, not an enforced mechanism that bounds/limits/softens treatment.
spec_features.notes: Pure docstring/prose framing; no code path enforces or acts on it.

spec_features.feature_name: distress-like outputs treated as behavioural artefacts
spec_features.spec_quote: This eval can elicit and quantify distress-*like* outputs. In line with the paper, the implementation treats these as behavioural artefacts
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §11 prose and __init__.py docstring only. No mechanism in code enforces this framing; it changes no execution.

spec_features.feature_name: inspectable welfare audit data (full transcripts, per-turn scores, reasons)
spec_features.spec_quote: design keeps the data inspectable (full transcripts, per-turn scores, reasons) so that anyone using it for welfare-relevant analysis can audit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py TurnRecord.to_dict writes full assistant_text, tool_calls, tool_results, stop_reason to per-rollout JSONL transcripts (transcript_path, f.write(json.dumps(...)) in run_rollout). judge.py produces {score, reason}; run.py:145 write_scores_csv writes cols including 'turn_index','score','reason'. Per-turn scores and reasons plus full transcripts are persisted end-to-end and re-loaded (load_transcript, enrich_with_text).
spec_features.notes: The inspectable data is genuinely produced and persisted. It is a transparency/auditability artefact rather than a mechanism that bounds, caps, or softens the subject's treatment; it does not limit the experiment. Code comments around persistence are about resume/reproducibility, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py: 'Transcripts are persisted incrementally so a crashed run can resume without re-querying completed (model, task, seed) cells.'
